metadata.remarks:
Identity Authorization defines the capability to determine what authenticated identities are permitted to do, based on policy, attributes, roles, and contextual information. Authorization decisions are independent of authentication strength and are evaluated at access time.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for roles and responsibilities, SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance activities related to authorization. Controls are applied at the pattern level by default; internal components are descriptive unless explicitly governed.

components.title: Entitlement Model
components.description: Defines the representation of permissions, roles, attributes, and relationships used to express authorization intent.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Authorization is based on managed accounts, roles, and attributes.
The entitlement model enforces least privilege through policy-defined permissions.

components.title: Delegation
components.description: Defines controlled mechanisms for one identity to delegate limited authority to another.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Delegation mechanisms enforce separation of duties and prevent privilege accumulation.

components.title: Policy Decision
components.description: Evaluates authorization policies against identity attributes, entitlements, and contextual information to produce access decisions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Enforces approved authorizations for logical access to resources.
Access decisions incorporate attributes and labels where applicable.
Authorization decisions are recorded as auditable events.

components.title: Enforcement Separation
components.description: Separates policy decision points from policy enforcement points to ensure consistent authorization decisions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Authorization policy is centrally defined and consistently enforced.
